# Installation

SEED-agent is installed like an OpenCode plugin package, while model provider
authentication remains owned by OpenCode. Normal users run the installer in the
repository they want SEED to work on; they do not clone the SEED Harness source
repository or connect a local source checkout to OpenCode.

## Runtime Requirements

- Linux. This release is distributed and validated for Linux only; Windows and
  macOS are not supported yet.
- Node.js `>=20`
- OpenCode CLI `>=1.15.6`
- Tested OpenCode CLI: `1.15.7`

The OpenCode CLI is installed outside this package, so SEED-agent enforces
compatibility through `doctor`. If a user has an older OpenCode CLI,
`doctor` exits with failure before they start relying on `/seed`.

## For Humans

Paste this into your LLM agent session from the repository where you want
`/seed` to work:

```text
Install and configure SEED Harness for the current project. Keep SEED model-neutral unless I explicitly ask to pin a model. First verify OpenCode is installed, then run the @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent installer for this project, tell me how to authenticate the OpenCode provider/model I want, run seed-agent doctor --project --agents, and tell me how to start /seed.
```

Or run the installer yourself:

```bash
cd <your-work-repo>
npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest install --project
opencode providers login -p <provider>
npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest doctor --project --agents
opencode
```

Inside OpenCode:

```text
/seed "Analyze this repository and tell me the run directory."
```

The installer registers a package plugin entry in OpenCode config and writes
SEED config for the current target project. It creates
`.opencode/opencode.jsonc` and `.opencode/seed-agent.jsonc` with model-neutral
SEED profiles, Lab-Representative, dynamic team tools, `/seed`, SEED MCP
defaults, and user skill roots disabled by default. By default, SEED inherits
the model selected in OpenCode for Lab-Representative. If a project wants to pin
one model for all SEED profiles, run the installer with `--model
provider/model`.
It also writes static project OpenCode agent and command entries instead of
relying only on the plugin config hook. The project config includes
`default_agent: "lab-representative"`, the Lab-Representative primary agent,
SEED command aliases, and disable stubs for native OpenCode `build`, `plan`,
`general`, `explore`, and `scout` entries unless host agents are explicitly
allowed.
For non-git workspaces, the installer writes the same OpenCode runtime defaults
to project-root `opencode.jsonc` as a compatibility config, because OpenCode may
load that file more reliably than walking into `.opencode/` before the project
has a git worktree.

After install, the OpenCode TUI should open on `Lab-Representative`. Dynamic
team member identities live in SEED run artifacts, not in the OpenCode agent
selector.

If OpenCode does not open on `Lab-Representative`, rerun the latest installer
in that target project:

```bash
npx @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest install --project
```

The installer normalizes the project SEED config to the current single
Lab-Representative shape and writes a `.bak-*` backup of the previous
`.opencode/seed-agent.jsonc`.

If Build/Plan still appears after reinstall, inspect parent directories for
inherited OpenCode config, for example `../.opencode/opencode.jsonc` or
another parent-directory OpenCode config. OpenCode merges parent project
configs, so a parent config can affect the current project.

## For LLM Agents

Follow these steps when helping a user install SEED Harness:

1. Check OpenCode:

   ```bash
   opencode --version
   ```

   If OpenCode is missing, ask the user to install it first from
   https://opencode.ai/docs. With npm available, the common install command is:

   ```bash
   npm install -g opencode-ai
   ```

2. Install SEED in the user's target repository. Do not clone the SEED Harness
   source repository for normal package installs.

   ```bash
   npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest install --project
   ```

3. Authenticate the provider the user wants to use through OpenCode:

   ```bash
   opencode providers login -p <provider>
   ```

4. Verify:

   ```bash
   npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest doctor --project --agents
   ```

5. Start OpenCode and tell the user to run `/seed`.

## Maintainer Local Checkout

Use this flow only when developing or validating SEED Harness itself from an
unpublished local checkout:

```bash
cd seed-harness
npm install
npm run build
node ./bin/seed-agent.js install --local --project
opencode providers login -p <provider>
node ./bin/seed-agent.js doctor --project --agents
```

`install --local --project` updates the project `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`
plugin list, creates `.opencode/seed-agent.jsonc` if it is missing, and
prepares `.opencode` plugin runtime dependencies for OpenCode. The generated
SEED config is model-neutral by default, ignores personal SEED user config for
project installs, disables personal user skill roots, and does not merge
host/user MCP servers by default. It does not create a model provider, does not
read API key values, and does not register a mock model.

## Verify

```bash
npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest doctor --project --agents
npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest run --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 --variant high "Create a short SEED trace smoke test and stop after reporting the run directory."
```

The expected healthy state is:

- OpenCode CLI is installed.
- SEED plugin is present in `opencode.jsonc`.
- SEED config is present or defaults are acceptable.
- If SEED config pins explicit models, those configured providers are visible to
  `opencode providers list`. If SEED config is model-neutral, `doctor` reports
  that the OpenCode selected provider/model will be used at runtime.
- Lab-Representative is registered through the primary agent id
  `lab-representative`.
- Native `Build` and `Plan` should not appear in the SEED project agent list
  after a current isolated project install.
- Dynamic team members are stored in SEED run artifacts, not in the OpenCode
  agent selector.

For an unpublished local checkout, replace
`npx --yes @seed-lab/opencode-seed-agent@latest` with
`node ./bin/seed-agent.js`.

## Provider Keys

Every user should run provider login on their own machine:

```bash
opencode providers login -p <provider>
```

Examples include `opencode providers login -p openai` for GPT models and
`opencode providers login -p anthropic` for Claude models. SEED-agent relies on
OpenCode for provider credentials and does not store model API keys. The plugin
trace redacts secrets, reasoning payloads, and raw host-tool output bodies by
default.

# MCP

Built-in MCP defaults:

- `context7`
- `lsp`
- `ast_grep`
- `websearch`
- `grep_app`

For reproducible project installs, the config hook publishes SEED MCP defaults
without merging existing host/user OpenCode MCP config. Set
`isolation.allow_host_mcp: true` only when you deliberately want host MCP
entries to participate; in that opt-in mode, existing `{ "enabled": false }`
entries remain disabled.

`websearch` is `auto` by default and is enabled only when `EXA_API_KEY` or `TAVILY_API_KEY` is available. `grep_app` is `auto` by default and can be enabled with `SEED_ENABLE_GREP_APP=1`.

`lsp` and `ast_grep` are enabled only when SEED can resolve local MCP CLIs from
the target repository or installed package ancestry:

- `packages/lsp-tools-mcp/dist/cli.js` or `packages/lsp-tools-mcp/src/cli.ts`
- `packages/ast-grep-mcp/dist/cli.js` or `packages/ast-grep-mcp/src/cli.ts`

If those CLIs are not present, SEED-agent registers the MCP entry as disabled and
adds `SEED_MCP_DIAGNOSTIC` to the local MCP environment. It does not fall back to
a fake server or to an unrelated `npx @ast-grep/cli mcp` command.

- Trace/evidence/telemetry/artifacts/policy: `seed_trace_event`, `seed_trace_read`, `seed_continuation_read`, `seed_context_bundle_list`, `seed_context_bundle_read`, `seed_context_metrics`, `seed_model_route`, `seed_run_telemetry`, `seed_artifact_list`, `seed_artifact_read`, `seed_policy_audit`, `seed_evidence_add`
- Orchestrator loop: `seed_orchestrator_next`, `seed_orchestrator_tick`, `seed_orchestrator_record_decision`

- Checks/scripts: `seed_tool_policy_check`, `seed_run_check`, `seed_run_script`, `seed_command_status`
- Background: `seed_background_start`, `seed_background_checkpoint`, `seed_background_notifications`, `seed_background_output`, `seed_background_followup`, `seed_background_cancel`
- Skills/media/documents/handoff: `seed_skill`, `seed_skill_recommend`, `seed_skill_mcp`, `seed_skill_validate`, `seed_browser_snapshot`, `seed_document_extract`, `seed_look_at`, `seed_handoff_to_professor`

Native OpenCode tools remain the file and shell execution surface; SEED does
not define `seed_edit`, `seed_write`, or a generic `seed_run` replacement.
The SEED tool list is manifest-backed: every `seed_*` tool has an explicit
surface category, and unrecognized future `seed_*` names fail closed for member
policy until the manifest is updated.
Powerful commands are screened for destructive patterns and should route through professor handoff when unsafe.
`seed_tool_policy_check` exposes the same allow/ask/deny command-policy decision
without executing the command. `seed_run_check`, `seed_run_script`, and
`seed_background_start` use that centralized policy before spawning tracked
verification or background processes. Those three command-execution tools are
reserved for the root Lab-Representative; ordinary members use native OpenCode
shell tools only when their contract, read/write paths, and leases allow it.
If OpenCode aborts a running command/background process, SEED kills the child
process, records the cancellation in trace/background state, and refreshes
continuation context.

Main SEED tasks can declare `depends_on`. `seed_task_update` refuses to move a
dependent task into `in_progress`, `review`, or `completed` until every listed
dependency task is completed. This keeps the professor-facing task board as
executable state instead of a loose checklist.

Coordinator-mode `/seed` runs treat Lab-Representative as the planner,
dispatcher, verifier, and reporter by default. The root Lab-Representative
session is blocked from direct native edit/write/bash writes unless it first
records a one-shot exception with `seed_coordinator_direct_work`. Dynamic member
sessions still use native tools through their member contract, write paths, and
workspace leases.

## Team Runtime

Team runtime tools persist state under `.seed-agent/runs/<run_id>/team/`.
Messages are delivered to per-member inboxes, acknowledgements are recorded,
member status is stored in `runtime.json`, and shared team tasks can be
created, claimed, released, updated, listed, and resumed. Claiming, blocking,
completing, cancelling, or releasing a team task refreshes the owner's durable
member status so `/seed-status`, continuation snapshots, and team tools see the
same shared state. Team tasks carry a monotonically increasing `revision`.
`seed_team_task_update` can pass `expected_revision`; if the current task has
moved on, SEED records a durable `stale_revision` conflict, blocks the task, and
keeps the stale patch from overwriting current owner, status, or evidence.
`seed_team_cleanup` completes the team runtime only after open team tasks and
unread team messages are resolved, then writes `team/cleanup.json` with task and
inbox counts. Use team tasks for coordination between lab members; use the main
SEED task board for the professor-facing acceptance path.

Team meeting tools create durable discussion threads under
`.seed-agent/runs/<run_id>/team/meetings/`. Use
`seed_team_meeting_create` when multiple members need to align on an agenda,
`seed_team_meeting_post` for messages, decisions, and action items, and
`seed_team_meeting_close` once the decision is summarized. Open meeting context
is injected into participant turns and continuation snapshots, while
`seed_team_broadcast` fans out a stateful announcement through member inboxes.

The orchestrator loop tools give Lab-Representative a durable coordinator
scratchpad under `.seed-agent/runs/<run_id>/orchestrator-loop.jsonl`.
`seed_orchestrator_next` computes the next action from mailbox, sub-plan,
meeting, and feedback-gate state; `seed_orchestrator_tick` records a loop tick;
and `seed_orchestrator_record_decision` records why the representative chose a
dispatch, wait, or verification step.
Tick and decision calls accept optional idempotency keys; repeated keys return a
deduplicated result instead of appending another coordinator event.

Ordinary members should not recursively spawn more agents by default. When a
member needs a new role, task, meeting, or delegation, it should call
`seed_team_member_request`; SEED records the request under
`team/member-requests.json` and sends a handoff message to Lab-Representative.
Direct delegation tools remain blocked for member sessions unless the durable
member `spawn_policy` explicitly allows it without Lab-Representative approval.

`seed_team_create` requires an explicit `inline_spec`. The core does not create
document-review, web-app, automation, or other domain rosters from
`workflow_template`. Lab-Representative can still include
`workflow_template.name` and required coverage as metadata inside the spec, but
the actual members, tool policy, write paths, evidence obligations, and stop
conditions must be present in the inline spec itself.

`seed_team_member_followup` targets an existing team member by role id and
continues that member's child session when it is idle, or leaves the message in
the durable mailbox when the member is busy. `seed_team_member_add` expands an
active dynamic team with a new inline member spec, validates the expanded
contract against max-member, policy, and write-path overlap rules, creates the
new inbox, launches a child session, and announces the join to the team.
Initial member launches and live follow-ups both send the member's resolved
OpenCode `tools` map with the prompt body. Each dynamic member is also recorded
as an agent-thread under `threads/threads.json`, with its tool manifest written
to `threads/<thread_id>/tool-manifest.json`. The same policy data is recorded
in `team/conversation.jsonl` as `session_tools`, alongside `allowed_tools`,
`denied_tools`, `allowed_skills`, `prompt_ref`, child session id, background
id, and agent-call metadata, so a later audit can verify what the member was
actually allowed to use.
Each member's durable contract is also reinjected into that member's future
model turns and compaction context so long-running sessions keep their role,
tool policy, MCP/skill policy, read/write scope, evidence obligations, and stop
condition even after context growth.
The same durable contract is enforced before tool execution: member sessions
cannot call denied or unlisted tools, and write/append workspace intents or
leases outside their `write_paths` are blocked and recorded in the trace.
Member-to-member communication uses durable message envelopes, not ad hoc
prompt copying: `seed_team_send` writes the recipient inbox, appends
`messages/envelopes.json`, records delivery attempts in `messages/delivery.jsonl`,
and appends `team/conversation.jsonl`; `seed_team_ack` marks consumed messages
and appends the acknowledgement. The conversation log is the quickest debug
path for reconstructing what the Lab-Representative asked each virtual member
to do and which messages were actually consumed. Use `seed_agent_thread_status`,
`seed_agent_thread_trace`, `seed_message_queue`, and `seed_team_conversation`
to read these logs from inside OpenCode. Entries include explicit `from` and
`to` fields plus launch ids, agent call ids, child session ids, background ids,
helper ids, prompt refs, delivery status, allowed/denied tools, MCP/skill
policy, read/write paths, and other member-contract metadata when available.
This is the primary ordered trace for Lab-Representative-to-member,
member-to-Lab-Representative, and member-to-member communication.
Message envelopes can also carry `context_refs` and `context_attachments`.
Use `seed_context_bundle_list` to see stored stable/warm/hot/heavy/memory
bundles, `seed_context_bundle_read` to inspect one bundle body, and
`seed_context_metrics` to see recent injection plans and budget counters.
These tools are read-only and safe for member sessions.

Sub-plans with `write_paths` must bind active write leases before entering
`executing`. Pass `subplan_id` to `seed_workspace_lease_acquire` to attach the
granted lease to the sub-plan, then use native OpenCode edit/write/bash tools
inside the member's allowed workspace. After the native write is verified,
record `seed_workspace_diff_record` with the changed paths, lease ids, and
sub-plan id; main-workspace diff records require active write-lease coverage for
their changed paths. Worktree-isolated sub-plans can execute without a main-workspace
lease, but their changes do not count as completed main-workspace work until
Lab-Representative or the sub-plan's `merge_owner_member` records
`seed_workspace_worktree_merge_record`. That merge record requires an active
main-workspace write lease covering the target paths, a worktree diff ref, and a
main-workspace diff ref. Out-of-scope worktree paths can be recorded as rejected
evidence without being merged. Final completion is blocked when required
accepted write sub-plans have no recorded diff ref, when a diff ref cannot be
found, when a recorded diff touches paths outside the sub-plan `write_paths`,
when a required worktree sub-plan lacks an applied merge record with both diff
refs, or when workspace conflicts remain open. Lease conflicts can open a
durable team meeting agenda so the decision and action items are available as
conflict-resolution evidence.

## Continuation Context

SEED writes compact continuation snapshots under
`.seed-agent/runs/<run_id>/continuation/`. The snapshot includes the active run,
open tasks, blockers, evidence refs, team unread counts, shared team tasks,
background work, pending background notifications, pending professor decisions, a prioritized `next_actions`
queue, and recent trace events. The plugin can inject this context into future
user turns and OpenCode compaction prompts when
`continuation` config is enabled. During OpenCode compaction, SEED adds only
runtime bridge context: continuation summary, team roster, open meetings,
member contract/memory, unread member mailbox, and background status. It does
not run a second compaction scheduler or summarizer. Background terminal states and professor
handoff requests refresh the snapshot immediately so the next agent turn sees
the latest decision point and the next concrete actions to take. Terminal
background work also creates durable parent-session notifications in
`background_notifications.json`; chat hooks can deliver those notices to the
parent session, and continuation snapshots keep them visible until delivery.

`seed_continuation_read` exposes the same continuation snapshot and prioritized
`next_actions` queue as a tool. By default it refreshes
`continuation/context.json` and `continuation/context.md` before returning the
machine-readable queue, so a worker can resume from durable state instead of
depending on hidden chat history.
Chat and compaction hooks store repeated continuation/team/member context in
the context ledger, then inject a bounded attachment plan. This preserves the
same durable resume information while reducing repeated raw prompt text.

Delegation tools create real OpenCode child sessions through the host SDK and run
the requested target agent. `seed_delegate_followup` continues an existing
child session by `session_id` or `background_id`; it does not create a new
session for a follow-up. Delegation resolves the target agent's model profile,
passes explicit `provider/model` routing when configured, retries configured
fallbacks on retryable model/provider failures, and records requested, resolved,
and attempted models in `agent_calls.jsonl`. Attempt records include immutable
`attempt_id`, `current`, and `stale` fields so retry history can be debugged
without confusing an old failed attempt with the current child-session state.
Delegation calls can also carry an optional `idempotency_key` for duplicate
dispatch detection. Session tools call OpenCode session APIs directly.
Use `seed_model_route` before unusual or high-risk delegation to inspect the
configured model profile, provider/model attempts, fallback count, and warnings
without launching a child session.
`seed_delegate` and `seed_delegate_background` can also receive
`skills: ["skill-name"]`. SEED loads those project/user `SKILL.md` files,
checks required MCP diagnostics, blocks the delegation when a required MCP is
unavailable, and otherwise injects a `<seed-skill-context>` block into the child
session prompt. They can also receive `auto_skills: true`; SEED then recommends
ready skills from the task prompt and target agent before launching the child
session. The injected skill bodies are stored as run artifacts and traced with
`delegation_skill_context_loaded`.
Background cancel sends `SIGTERM` to spawned processes or aborts OpenCode child
sessions; it is not a trace-only marker.

Use `seed_background_checkpoint` for long-running work. A checkpoint observes
the current child session once, records status in the run trace, appends a short
progress note, and returns the next action. It does not wait indefinitely,
cancel the work, or treat long duration as failure.

Use `seed_background_followup` when the professor intervenes while an OpenCode
background child session is still running. It sends the intervention into the
existing child session with `promptAsync`, records `background_followup_sent`,
and updates `background_tasks.json` so `/seed-status` shows the latest
intervention. Process background tasks cannot receive prompt follow-ups; for
those tasks the tool records the message and returns `recorded_only`.

`seed_background_output` can return either the compact output tail or a filtered
full child-session transcript:

```jsonc
{
  "background_id": "bg_...",
  "full_session": true,
  "since_message_id": "msg_...",
  "include_tool_results": true,
  "message_limit": 50
}
```

`seed_background_notifications` lists durable pending, delivered, or dismissed
background completion notices. Use it when resuming a long run to see which
background child sessions still need parent review before reading full output.

`seed_run_telemetry` builds a structured quality summary for a run. It reads
the run state, tasks, events, agent calls, tool calls, evidence ledger, and
final report; writes `artifacts/run-telemetry.json`; and returns task/tool/agent
counts, model-attempt counts, evidence coverage, and quality-gate warnings.

`seed_artifact_list` reads the versioned artifact index at
`artifacts/index.json`. Artifacts written by SEED tools are indexed with schema
version, relative path, extension, size, and timestamps. If an older run has
artifact files but no index, reading the index initializes it from the existing
artifact directory.
`seed_artifact_read` reads one indexed artifact by `artifact_id` or relative
path, returns bounded text content, emits an `artifact_read` trace event, and
runs the policy audit on the artifact content so replayed evidence remains
inspectable and safety-checked.

`seed_policy_audit` checks final report, progress, evidence, or provided text
for secret-looking values, machine-specific local paths, and
prompt-injection-like text. It writes `artifacts/policy-audit.json`. When
`safety.redact_secrets` is enabled, `seed_report_write` with
`status: "completed"` blocks final reports that contain secret or local-path
policy findings before the run can be closed.

`seed_report_check` checks `final_report.md` or provided report content against
the evidence ledger and task evidence refs, then writes
`artifacts/report-gate.json`. When `run.review_before_final` is enabled,
`seed_report_write` with `status: "completed"` enforces the same gate before it
writes the final report or closes the run. Exceptional professor-approved cases
can pass `bypass_review_gate: true`, but the default path requires cited
`evidence.md#...` anchors.

`seed_skill` loads `SKILL.md` files from project skill directories such as
`.seed-agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. User skill directories are also available
when `skills.allow_user_skills` is enabled. Loaded skills return their source,
metadata, body, artifact `content_ref`, required/optional MCP declarations, and
MCP diagnostics. `seed_skill_recommend` ranks discoverable skills for a task
query, target agent, and optional category using `name`, `description`,
`keywords`, `triggers`, `tags`, `agents`, `categories`, and required MCP
readiness. It writes the recommendation set as a run artifact. `seed_skill_mcp`
returns the workspace MCP inventory or the
same requirement diagnostics for one skill. `seed_skill_validate` statically
checks project skills for metadata, duplicate names, empty bodies, and required
MCP availability, then writes a JSON validation report artifact. User skill
validation is opt-in with `include_user: true` so project checks stay
reproducible in fresh clones.

`seed_browser_snapshot` launches a bounded headless browser capture path for a
local file, or for an external http(s) URL only when the call explicitly sets
`allow_external: true`. It uses an isolated temporary browser profile, writes a
`type: "seed.browser_snapshot"` JSON artifact, stores a PNG screenshot artifact
when the browser provides one, and immediately routes the snapshot through
`seed_look_at` inspection so the result lands in the evidence ledger. A custom
browser command is allowed only when the executable name is a known
Chromium/Firefox browser or the call explicitly sets
`allow_custom_browser_command: true`. Captured HTML is reduced to visible text
with simple hidden-element stripping before it becomes browser snapshot text;
hidden text, ARIA/title prompt-injection cues, and unsafe URL references remain
recorded as security findings.

`seed_document_extract` is the local PDF text-ingestion path. It shells out to
`pdftotext`, honoring `SEED_PDFTOTEXT_BIN` first and `PDFTOTEXT_BIN` as a
compatibility alias, then PATH. It writes metadata, extractor, normalized text,
page JSONL, chunk JSONL, and extraction-report artifacts under
`artifacts/documents/<document_id>/`, indexes each artifact, records evidence,
and reports Linux-focused recovery guidance when `pdftotext` is unavailable.
That guidance is intentionally non-deterministic: Lab-Representative should
inspect the distro, package manager, PATH, sudo behavior, network/policy
constraints, and package candidates before proposing or running any install
command. Any side-effecting install must still go through SEED/OpenCode policy
gates. If installation is blocked, Lab-Representative should record the blocker
and the exact admin command to run. Set `SEED_PDFTOTEXT_BIN` to an explicit
`pdftotext` binary path when PATH does not expose it.

`seed_look_at` inspects supported local images, screenshots, PDFs, text
documents such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, and JSON, and browser snapshot JSON
files with `type: "seed.browser_snapshot"`. It records file provenance, MIME
type, size, SHA-256, extracted findings, an artifact JSON, and an evidence
entry. Text document and browser snapshot inspection also run the SEED policy
audit so prompt-injection-like instructions, secrets, or local-path leaks are
recorded as evidence findings rather than followed as operator instructions.
Browser snapshot content is always marked `browser_snapshot_untrusted`, and a
linked `screenshot_path` is checked as a local image with size, hash, MIME, and
dimension metadata. External URLs are not fetched by `seed_look_at`; they are
marked as untrusted unless a separate `seed_browser_snapshot` capture has already
materialized them into a local snapshot artifact. Text and browser snapshot
artifacts also include a `seed.trust_boundary` envelope summary for untrusted
content. The envelope escapes nested boundary markers, reports warning counts,
and redacts configured `security_canaries` when recording excerpts; matching
canary tokens fail the policy audit as `no_canary_token_leak`.
For PDFs, `seed_look_at` remains a quick provenance/metadata inspection. Use
`seed_document_extract` when a document/PDF task needs page and chunk artifacts
that a final report can cite.

Persistent browser sessions are intentionally not enabled yet. The planned
sidecar boundary, lifecycle state, security policy, and eval requirements are
tracked in `docs/browser-media-sidecar.md`.

# Trace Artifacts

Every run writes to `.seed-agent/runs/<run_id>/`. Reusable professor guidance is
stored across runs under `.seed-agent/memory/`.

- `.seed-agent/memory/MEMORY.md`: human-readable index of reusable professor
  memory.
- `.seed-agent/memory/items/<memory_id>.json`: source, kind, why, and
  how-to-apply fields for a durable professor memory item.

- `run.json`: versioned run metadata, state revision, status, model, goal, artifacts.
- `tasks.json`: versioned explicit task board owned by `lab-representative`.
- `events.jsonl`: append-only lifecycle timeline.
- `agent_calls.jsonl`: child-session calls and delegation records.
- `model_calls.jsonl`: append-only model attempt records derived from
  delegation/follow-up calls, including fallback status, resolved model,
  prompt artifact ref, and sanitized result/error summaries.
- `budget.json`: run safety budget state: elapsed-runtime limit, child session
  limit, model-call limit, warning threshold, stale-worker threshold, observed
  child sessions, model calls, token usage and cost buckets when OpenCode
  exposes them, and context injection counters.
- `background_tasks.json`: long-running background process/session status and checkpoints.
- `background_notifications.json`: durable parent-session notices for completed, failed, or cancelled background work.
- `team/runtime.json`: durable team member/status state, dynamic team id/name,
  launch status, member session ids, background ids, prompt refs, and cleanup
  instructions for partial launch failures.
- `team/specs/<team_id>.json`: accepted dynamic team spec contract before
  launch.
- `team/specs/<team_id>.md`: human-readable rendering of the accepted dynamic
  team spec.
- `team/tasks.json`: shared team task board with ownership, dependencies, revisions, and stale-update conflict records.
- `team/inbox/<member>/*.json`: durable per-member team messages and acknowledgement state.
- `threads/threads.json`: canonical agent-thread records. Each dynamic member
  is represented as a durable thread with session/background ids, prompt refs,
  tool/skill/MCP policy, helper budget, helper counts, and memory refs.
- `threads/<thread_id>/tool-manifest.json`: exact tool/skill/MCP/read/write
  manifest assigned to that thread.
- `threads/<thread_id>/helpers.jsonl`: append-only helper child-session ledger
  owned by that thread.
- `messages/envelopes.json`: durable agent-to-agent message envelopes with
  `from`, `to`, body/prompt refs, correlation ids, allowed tools/skills, target
  session ids, context refs/attachments, delivery status, retries, and errors.
- `messages/delivery.jsonl`: append-only delivery attempts for live
  `promptAsync`, mailbox-only, retry, and failure outcomes.
- `team/conversation.jsonl`: ordered team communication audit log with explicit
  `from`/`to`, launch/follow-up entries, prompt refs, child session ids,
  background ids, allowed/denied tools, and the OpenCode `session_tools` map
  sent to member sessions when available.
- `workspace/intents.json`: declared read/write/append intentions before lease
  acquisition.
- `workspace/leases.json`: active, blocked, and released workspace leases.
- `workspace/conflicts.json`: open/resolved lease overlaps and stale base-hash
  conflicts that can block final completion.
- `workspace/diffs.json`: recorded changed-path summaries used as write
  evidence for sub-plan verification and final completion gates.
- `workspace/merges.json`: worktree merge records that tie an isolated
  worktree diff to the accepted main-workspace diff under a main-workspace
  write lease.
- `context/bundles.json`: index of cache-aware context bundles with category,
  scope, owner, digest, body ref, byte length, and SHA-256.
- `context/bodies/<bundle_id>.md`: stored context body for stable contracts,
  warm summaries, hot deltas, heavy artifact refs, or memory checkpoints.
- `context/metrics.jsonl`: append-only context planning/render metrics used by
  `seed_context_metrics` and budget context counters.
- `continuation/context.json`: machine-readable continuation snapshot for
  resume, compaction, pending decisions, prioritized next actions, open
  sub-plans, budget warnings, stale background work, professor memory refs,
  terminal background work, and pending background notifications.
- `continuation/context.md`: compact continuation context injected into future
  turns when enabled.
- `meetings/state.json`: durable manual Lab Meeting state after
  `/seed-lab-meeting` is used.
- `meetings/<meeting_id>.json`: machine-readable Lab Meeting feedback-gate
  summary.
- `meetings/<meeting_id>.md`: professor-facing Lab Meeting summary and
  feedback options.
- `tool_calls.jsonl`: tool/MCP/command audit records.
- `evidence.md`: human-readable evidence ledger with stable anchors.
- `progress.md`: live professor-facing status.
- `final_report.md`: final professor-facing report.
- `activity/README.md`: index for the human-readable activity journal.
- `activity/latest.md`: latest Lab-Representative briefing for quick
  inspection.
- `activity/latest.json`: machine-readable latest RepresentativeBriefing.
- `activity/<10-minute-window>.md`: synthesized professor-facing briefing for
  the configurable time bucket. The default bucket size is 10 minutes.
- `activity/<10-minute-window>.json`: machine-readable RepresentativeBriefing
  for that bucket.
- `activity/raw/<10-minute-window>.md`: raw chronological sanitized event,
  agent-call, and tool-call summaries for audit/debugging.
- `artifacts/`: command output, prompts, exported material, and generated
  summaries such as `run-telemetry.json`, `report-gate.json`, and
  `policy-audit.json`.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/metadata.json`: local PDF provenance,
  byte size, SHA-256, trust classification, and resolved source path.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/extractor.json`: `pdftotext` binary path,
  flavor, version, OS details, normalization flags, page/chunk counts,
  warnings, and confidence.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/text.txt`: normalized extracted PDF text.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/pages.jsonl`: page-level untrusted text
  records.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/chunks.jsonl`: chunk-level citation
  records for document/PDF analysis.

For tiny smoke tasks, the Lab-Representative can complete the work directly
after recording the reason with `seed_orchestrator_record_decision` and, for
native write/bash work in coordinator mode, `seed_coordinator_direct_work`.
That is why `agent_calls.jsonl` can be empty and `team/runtime.json` can list
only the lead member. A real dynamic team launch is visible in
`agent_calls.jsonl`, `team/runtime.json`, `team/launch-ledger.jsonl`, and
`team/conversation.jsonl`. Use `seed_team_conversation` for a readable timeline;
its timeline lines include `from -> to`, prompt refs, agent-call/session ids,
and `session_tools:<tool>=on/off` when the tool map was part of the launch or
follow-up.
- `artifacts/report-gate*.json`: final-completion gate output. Besides
  evidence-anchor checks, the gate records referenced HTML artifacts, detects
  placeholder/TODO text and missing files, and blocks completion while member
  threads, helpers, or background sessions are still open or failed.
- `artifacts/documents/<document_id>/extraction-report.md`: professor-facing
  extraction summary and trust-boundary warning.
- `artifacts/index.json`: versioned artifact index with relative paths, file
  metadata, and timestamps for generated run artifacts, including accepted
  team specs outside the `artifacts/` folder.

JSON and JSONL are the source of truth. Markdown is derived professor-facing material.
The activity journal is event-driven: it appends to a raw current time bucket
when SEED observes command, message, tool, delegation, evidence, team,
background, or continuation activity, then regenerates the current
Lab-Representative briefing from the trace, team state, workspace state,
artifacts, and blockers. It does not claim to expose hidden model reasoning.
Mailbox live-delivery attempts are recorded as events such as
`team_member_woken` or `team_member_wake_failed`; mailbox-only delivery remains
visible through the inbox files and unread counts in team status. Message
transform injection is derived from `team/runtime.json`, `team/tasks.json`, and
`team/inbox/` and does not create a second source of truth.
Lab Meetings are manual professor feedback gates. `/seed-lab-meeting` writes the
meeting state, asks active background workers to finish their already-assigned
background sessions, waits for those sessions to become terminal, and blocks new
delegation, team launch, and write/append workspace leases while the meeting is
wrapping up or awaiting feedback. Professor feedback is recorded through the
next normal Lab-Representative chat message, not a separate resume command.
`run.json`, `active-run.json`, task records, and `artifacts/index.json` include
schema versions. `run.json` and `active-run.json` also include
`state_revision`, which increments through the SEED mutation helper on
high-value state updates. JSONL trace appends are file-lock serialized. Legacy
v0 run/task state is migrated to the current schema when the harness reads it.
Older run artifact folders without an index are indexed on read so generated
outputs remain discoverable.

## Black-Box Fixture

`npm run e2e:blackbox` runs the fixture definitions in `evals/black-box/`
through SEED's public tool and command surfaces with an OpenCode-like host
client. The basic fixture verifies `final_report.md`, JSONL trace, the activity
journal, `artifacts/index.json`, and a captured host/tool transcript together.
The document/PDF fixture additionally drives `seed_team_create` with an
explicit inline spec, `seed_document_extract`, workspace leases,
representative briefings, `model_calls.jsonl`, and
`/seed-lab-meeting` plus normal professor feedback chat.
The Claude runtime UX fixture exercises the full professor-facing loop:
dynamic planner/implementer/verifier members, `team/launch-ledger.jsonl`,
`team/conversation.jsonl`, required sub-plan rework and acceptance, native
write-hook denial outside a member lease, duplicate-safe idempotency records,
stale team-task conflict handling, Lab Meeting feedback, budget state, and
untrusted document-evidence envelopes.
It is an example fixture for the generic dynamic-team path, not a built-in
paper-specific product mode.
Set `SEED_BLACK_BOX_E2E_KEEP=1` to preserve the temporary target repository and
transcript for manual inspection. Set `SEED_BLACK_BOX_E2E_OUT=<dir>` to write
partial JSONL progress and a final `black-box-results.json` collector report
that can be compared with the previous run in the same directory.
